To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Kif23-CHO1 is phosphorylated on two LATS kinase consensus sites by NDR/LATS kinases, with the upstream S716 site being required for efficient phosphorylations on the S814 14-3 binding site.

Kif23-CHO1 contains two NDR/LATS kinases consensus sites, that are phosphorylated in vitro and in vivo by NDR and/or LATS kinases, and that phosphorylation of these sites is required for efficient Kif23-cho1/iso1-14-3-binding.

phosphorylation of S716 and S814 in CHO1 is regulated by sequential NDR/LATS kinases, and that phosphorylation of these two sites is essential to regulate the interaction between 14-3.3 and Kif23, and that this interaction plays a role in regulating Kif23 localization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the Kif23/CHO1 isoform, a key player in cytokinesis.

the identification of the kinases involved in the phosphorylation at the HXRXXS/LATS/NDR consensus sites of Kif23, the identification of the regulatory mechanisms involved in the phosphorylations at these sites, and their functional relevance.

the phosphorylation of two HXRXXST/LATS kinase consensus phosphosites in Kif23, revealing that the phosphorylation of these sites is differentially regulated in the two Kif isoforms, and that this is required for efficient Kif-14-3 interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Kif23-CHO1, but not Kif23-MKLP1, contains an NDR/LATS phosphorylation site at S716, that this site regulates the efficiency of Kif23 phosphorylation at the LATS consensus site at S814, and that the S814 site is phosphorylated by LATS kinases and binds 14-3.3 proteins, thus regulating the clustering of Kif23 during cytokinesis.

the Kif23-CHO1 isoform is the most important isoform, since it is the only one to be expressed in the midbody and it is the one that is phosphorylated at S716, which in turn is required for efficient LATS-mediated phosphorylation of S814, which is required for efficient 14-3 binding, which in turn plays a role in cytokinesis.

Kif23 phosphorylation by NDR and/or LATS kinases is a complex process, involving multiple phosphorylation steps, and that this phosphorylation regulates 14-3-binding and Kif23 clustering in cytokinetic midbodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of Kif23 is an essential mechanism for regulating Kif23 clustering at midbody, a process that is required for the completion of cytokinesis.

the two HXRXXXS/T LATS consensus sites on Kif23, present in the longest CHO1 isoform, are phosphorylated sequentially, with the most C-terminal site S814 playing a key role in the regulation of Kif3-14-3 binding, which is essential for Kif3 localization and activity during cytokinesis.

phosphorylation of Kif23 on S814 is regulated by sequential NDR/LATS phosphorylations at S716 and S814, and this phosphorylation plays a role during cytokinesis, possibly in the regulation of Kif-23 clustering at midbody.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the regulation of Kif3-iso1/CH1 interaction with 14-3 proteins by sequential NDR/LATS kinases-dependent phosphorylation provides an additional mechanism to ensure the robust and timely execution of cytokinesis.

Kif23 phosphorylation is tightly regulated by sequential phosphorylation of two NDR/LATS sites, and that this regulation has important implications for the role of 14-3 in the function of Kif23 during cytokinesis.
